rationale: The workflow already applies the relevant optimizations supported by the evidence: it uses concurrency with cancel-in-progress for the pages group, and the mise action already enables cache: true for dependency/tool installation (covering the dependency-cache pattern). The remaining candidate patterns are not suitable: P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE lists release/deployment work as a contraindication and this workflow deploys to GitHub Pages; P-LIT-IDLE-SCHEDULE and P-LIT-FAIL-SCHEDULE require schedule triggers which this workflow lacks; P-LIT-FAIL-FAST requires a matrix; P-LIT-CHANGE-FILTER is risky for a deployment workflow where configuration or content changes can affect the entire site; P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT lacks sufficient representative history and runs are consistently fast (~30s), so a timeout would be a safety bound rather than a meaningful optimization. No additional evidence-supported change preserves coverage while providing a clear benefit.
